crs_note: British National Grid, exactly as Margate. Every raster and vector in the pipeline is held in this CRS; OSM arrives in WGS84 degrees and is reprojected by step 01.
crs_max_transform_accuracy_note: Inherited from Margate. Step 01 refuses to reproject OSM unless PROJ's best WGS84 -> OSGB36 operation is at least this accurate: the OSTN15 grid (1 m class), not the 2 m Helmert fallback that put the Margate model 1.8 m off the LIDAR. The grid is not installed on this machine; step 01 sets PROJ_NETWORK=ON and PROJ fetches it from cdn.proj.org.
origin_note: South-west corner of the tile grid, in CRS metres. Chosen so that Margate's grid (origin 632800/168200) is a sub-grid: Margate tile (i, j) == Thanet tile (i+10, j+10). Margate's 91 downloaded tile positions (182 rasters) are therefore bit-identical to what step 02 would fetch here and are copied in by sources/fetch/reuse_tiles.py instead of re-downloaded.
grid_res_note: Samples per tile edge. 513 = 512 + 1 so adjacent tiles share an identical edge row and there is no seam. Extent: E 627680..640992, N 163080..172808 (13.3 x 9.7 km, 494 tile positions).
bbox_note: S,W,N,E -- Overpass order. Generous on purpose: the grid and the clip are the model; features outside them are counted and dropped by steps 06/07/10/11. Expect a ~45 MB extract (Margate's 8.6 MB scaled by area).

clip.note: The Isle of Thanet is cut from the mainland by a hard straight line along the old Wantsum Channel. A point P is KEPT iff cross(B-A, P-A) >= 0, i.e. (P-A) . (6071, 6984) >= 0 -- the half-plane on the LEFT of A->B, which is north-east. Points exactly on the line are kept. Step 02 does not fetch tiles wholly outside; step 05 writes nodata (not filled) for cells outside; steps 06/07/09/10/11 drop and count. Endpoints are config, not code: move them and rebuild.
clip.endpoints_note: A = Minnis Bay, B = Pegwell Bay: a HAND-CHOSEN straight line along the old Wantsum Channel, DEFINED by the WGS84 positions 51.38015 N 1.28241 E and 51.32281 N 1.37858 E. Those lat/lons are the definition, not a citation: checked 2026-09-08 against data/thanet/raw/thanet.osm (222,200 nodes, 41,906 ways), the extract contains NO node tagged natural=bay and NO node tagged place=locality anywhere, and nothing tagged within 200 m of B -- an earlier version of this note claimed both endpoints were such nodes and that was wrong. Reprojected through the OSTN15 grid (PROJ_NETWORK=ON cs2cs EPSG:4326 EPSG:27700, PROJ operation 'Inverse of OSGB36 to WGS 84 (9) + British National Grid, 1 m'), the same operation step 01 uses, they are 628512.049/169679.539 and 635496.568/163608.977; clip.line stores them ROUNDED TO THE METRE, which moves A by 0.46 m, B by 0.57 m and the line itself by at most 0.36 m perpendicular. That rounding, not the datum, is the residual error in the cut position -- everything downstream is self-consistent with the stored integers. The Helmert fallback gives 628514/169681 and 635498/163610, about 2 m away, and MUST NOT be used (dryrun.py check 'C-lib thanet.json clip.line == BRIEF 4.1'). Stored line: 9,253.8 m, bearing 131.0 deg A->B. Verified kept: Margate, Birchington station, Manston, Ramsgate harbour, North Foreland. Verified excluded: Minster, Cliffsend.
clip.budget_note: Against this 26x19 grid, by tile corners: 360 tiles inside, 31 straddle, 103 outside -> 391 tiles fetched (782 rasters); 3,861,822 of the 8,158,239 cell centres of the straddle tiles lie outside and are written as NoData by step 05. Recomputed by dryrun.py check 'C-lib tile_state / cell_mask on the Thanet grid' against this file.

vertical_datum_note: Ordnance Datum Newlyn -- the datum of the EA LIDAR. Every elevation the pipeline emits, including water_level, is metres above this.
water_level_note: INHERITED FROM MARGATE (same EA composite, same survey flights, same chalk coast; measured there as the DTM's flat sea surface). Expected to hold across the isle. Check coast_manifest.water_tiles and the sea-tile minima from the first Thanet run of 05 before trusting it for Pegwell Bay's mudflats.

height_calib.note: mode auto: step 07 regresses height = intercept + m_per_level * building:levels from THANET's own buildings that carry both a levels tag and a trustworthy LIDAR p50, records the fit in massing_manifest.json, and uses it. The fallback is Margate's FITTED line (n=1457, 83 rejected, rmse 1.4 m, measured 2026-09-07 on this same survey). With ~4x Margate's building stock the fit will engage; the manifest says source=fitted if it did.

coast.note: INHERITED FROM MARGATE. foreshore_max_odn is a property of the survey's tide state: the EA flew this stretch at low tide, so the intertidal flat reads as land and anything below 1.2 m ODN is sand. rock_slope_deg is the ramp tuned to the Cliftonville chalk cliffs; Thanet is the same chalk from Birchington round North Foreland to Ramsgate. Clipped tiles (outside the Wantsum line) are NOT missing tiles -- they are listed separately as tiles_clipped.
coast.missing_tiles_are_water_note: MEASURED on the first Thanet run (2026-09-08) and re-measured from the products 2026-09-08, not inherited: unlike Margate and Whitby, the composite runs out far offshore here. Step 09 lists 35 grid positions with under 1% DTM coverage as tiles_without_dtm -- j=18 for i=0..16, j=17 for i=2..8, j=16 for i=2, i=25 for j=0..6 and i=24 for j=0..2 -- open sea north of the isle and south-east of Ramsgate, whose neighbouring tiles bottom out at -3.0..-1.6 m ODN (the surveyed sea surface). They are therefore added to water_tiles (192 of them; every tiles_without_dtm position is in that list). Read coast_manifest.tiles_without_dtm for the authoritative set: this prose is a description, the manifest is the record. A subset of 28 of those positions has no valid cell AT ALL and is exported by step 05 as a flat plate at water_level (fill 'all-nodata -> -0.6', listed as tiles_fabricated in terrain_manifest.json): j=18 for i=0..15, j=17 for i=2..7, i=25 for j=0..4 and i=24 for j=2. Nothing in those 7,368,732 cells was surveyed. The inherited water_level -0.6 is the UPPER bound of the water band, so the plate still sits ~2 m above the deep-water surface its neighbours carry; the deep water itself is caught by the below-water-level rule (water tiles' minima: p5 -2.98, p50 -2.70, p95 -1.08 m). If the offshore ledge shows in a render, the honest fix is a measured offshore water surface for this site, not a different fabricated constant.

wcs.note: Identical to Margate's -- a precondition for reusing its tiles (reuse_tiles.py refuses if either coverage differs).

lidar_reuse_note: Before step 02: PY sources/fetch/reuse_tiles.py --from margate --to thanet. It proves both grids are 512-aligned with identical tile_m, grid_res, crs and WCS coverages, copies data/margate/raw/lidar/{dtm,dsm}_x{i}_y{j}.tif to data/thanet/raw/lidar/{dtm,dsm}_x{i+10}_y{j+10}.tif after checking each file's own georeferencing tag lands where the new name says, and writes the four-key _grid.json stamp so step 02 accepts the directory and fetches only the remaining 300 tile positions.

landmarks._note: INHERITED FROM MARGATE (both are on the isle). Hand-authored overrides for buildings the LIDAR p50 estimator gets wrong, keyed by OSM name; step 07 reports how many applied. Do NOT pre-add Ramsgate or Broadstairs landmarks: qa_height_outliers.json from the first Thanet run decides whether the Royal Harbour buildings, Bleak House or the Granville need one.

Arlington House.why: 18-storey tower on a large podium; p50 samples the podium (7.0m from 22px). Real height ~57m.

Jubilee Clock Tower.why: MEASURED 2026-09-08 against the Thanet mosaics, OSM way 589052636: over the 22 footprint cells DSM max 21.45 - DTM p50 6.49 = 14.96 m, nDSM p90 14.49 m, and the way's own OSM height tag says 14. Three independent numbers agree on ~15 m. The value inherited from margate.json was 24.0 with the unevidenced reason 'Real height ~24m', i.e. +9 m on a hero landmark; the override is kept only because the tiny footprint (7 px above min_pixels) makes the p50 rung read 12.1 m and because roof=tower is worth stating.
